items.title: MAJOR INCIDENT: Major Off-Airport Aircraft Crash Mobilizes Massive Emergency Response
items.location: Shepperdine Road, BS35 1RJ Oldbury on Severn
items.summary: A Major Incident has been declared following a large off-airport aircraft crash on Shepperdine Road in Oldbury on Severn, with emergency services treating 103 potential patients.
items.body:
A MAJOR INCIDENT has been declared in South Gloucestershire following a catastrophic off-airport aircraft crash on Shepperdine Road, Oldbury on Severn (BS35 1RJ). First responders arrived on scene to find widespread debris and active fuel fires, initiating an urgent, large-scale multi-agency rescue and medical response to assist 103 patients.
A massive taskforce composed of regional fire, police, health, and specialist response teams has been deployed to secure the incident ground, combat extensive fires, and carry out complex extrication and triage operations:
 15 Fire Engines & 5 Foam Units: Supplying continuous high-volume fire suppression and specialist foam bladders to extinguish aviation fuel blazes.
 4 Water Carriers: Ensuring an uninterrupted water supply to rural ground units.
 5 Rescue Support Vehicles: Equipped with heavy hydraulic cutting, lifting, and stabilization gear for immediate airframe extrications.
 1 Breathing Apparatus Support Unit: Supplying fresh air cylinders and specialized breathing apparatus to support sustained crew operations in heavy smoke.
 4 HazMat Units / CBRN Vehicles: Monitoring air safety, hazardous materials, and containment of leaked aviation fluids.
 12 Fire Officers & 2 ICCU / Ambulance Control Units: Establishing multi-agency tactical command posts to coordinate scene operations and radio logistics.
 1 Mass Casualty Equipment Unit: Setting up field triage centers, medical shelters, and emergency supplies to support 103 casualties.
 1 Ambulance Officer & 3 Operational Team Leaders: Directing ground paramedics, prioritizing critical patients, and organizing rapid air/ground evacuations.
 2 PRVs (Patient Response Vehicles) & 2 SRVs (Specialist Response Vehicles): Supplying advanced life support, trauma response, and rapid paramedic intervention.
 1 ATV Carrier: Deploying all-terrain vehicles to transport medical crews and rescue equipment across difficult rural terrain.
 2 Welfare Vehicles: Providing essential hydration, nutrition, and rest facilities for emergency personnel on scene.
 12 Police Cars & 1 Police Helicopter: Enforcing extensive road closures around Shepperdine Road, securing the outer crash perimeter, and providing aerial reconnaissance for search operations.
Emergency services remain on site in full operation. Residents in Oldbury on Severn and the surrounding areas are strongly advised to keep clear of all main access roads to allow blue-light vehicles uninterrupted access to the casualty area.

items.title: Major Aircraft Incident Declared Near Bristol Airport Following Code F Emergency
items.summary: Emergency services have initiated a massive multi-agency response following a Code F aircraft accident near North Side Road in Wrington, involving 180 patients.
items.body:
A major incident has been declared near Bristol Airport following a Code F aircraft accident on North Side Road, Wrington (BS40 9UU). Emergency services were alerted to the incident after an aircraft encountered a severe collision emergency, prompting an immediate mobilization of airport fire services, local authorities, and regional health trusts to manage 180 potential patients on scene.
A vast multi-agency force has been deployed to secure the site, execute structural and foam suppression tactics, and provide critical medical triage:
 10 Fire Engines / Major Foam Tenders & 5 Major Foam Tenders: Supplying continuous high-volume foam bladders and suppression to manage aviation fuel hazards.
 1 Aerial Appliance Truck / Rescue Stairs: Assisting with high-level access and patient evacuation from the airframe.
 2 Rescue Support Vehicles: Providing specialized heavy cutting, lifting, and rescue extraction equipment.
 1 Water Carrier: Ensuring continuous water supplies for persistent foam generation and site cooling.
 2 HazMat Units / CBRN Vehicles: Monitoring aviation fuel vapor levels, hazardous materials, and environmental runoff.
 1 Airfield Firefighting Command Vehicle & 6 Fire Officers / Command Vehicles: Establishing operational sectors and directing multi-point firefighting tactics.
 1 ICCU / Ambulance Control Unit: Serving as the central tactical headquarters for scene coordination and triage management.
 1 Mass Casualty Equipment Unit: Supplying field treatment tents, stretchers, and emergency medical kits for large-scale patient care.
 4 Airfield Operations Vehicles & 2 Airfield Operations Supervisors: Overseeing airside security, perimeter access, and runway/airfield logistics.
 1 Ambulance Officer & 5 Operational Team Leaders: Directing ground paramedics and rapid-triage operations for 180 casualties.
 4 PRVs (Patient Response Vehicles) & 4 SRVs (Specialist Response Vehicles): Providing immediate advanced life support and fast-response paramedic care.
 2 Welfare Vehicles: Supporting emergency personnel with supplies, hydration, and operational rotation gear.
 12 Police Cars & 6 Traffic Cars: Enforcing road closures across North Side Road, maintaining blue-light routes, and securing the main incident perimeter.
Specialist medical units are prioritizing patient stabilization and transport. Members of the public are strictly advised to avoid the North Side Road and surrounding Wrington access routes to ensure emergency vehicles maintain unimpeded access.

items.title: Inshore Lifeboat Dispatched to Dis-Masted Boat Near Cardiff Bay Barrage
items.location: Cardiff Bay Barrage, CF64 1FP Penarth Marina
items.summary: An Inshore Lifeboat (ILB) was launched to assist a dis-masted sailing boat caught in difficulty near the Cardiff Bay Barrage at Penarth Marina.
items.body:
Emergency volunteer crews were called into action at 19:17 following reports of a dis-masted sailing boat in distress near the Cardiff Bay Barrage (CF64 1FP). The vessel lost its rigging and mast, leaving it immobilized and drifting close to the barrage perimeter near Penarth Marina as dusk approached.
An Inshore Lifeboat (ILB) was deployed to assess the situation and render aid to the stranded vessel:
 1 Inshore Lifeboat (ILB): Dispatched to navigate the shallow coastal waters, establish a towline, stabilize the vessel, and safeguard the crew on board.
Volunteer lifeboat crew members arrived on scene to secure the vessel's tangled rigging, prevent further damage from the submerged mast, and ensure the vessel was brought safely into calmer waters. No major injuries were reported, and normal transit through the barrage locks remains clear.

items.title: Major Underground Electrical Cable Fire Causes Substantial Disruption in Central London
items.summary: Underground electrical cable fire in central London with multi-agency response and substantial disruption.
items.body: Emergency services are dealing with a major underground electrical cable fire in central London. Fire crews are in attendance with specialist resources. Roads in the immediate area are closed and there is disruption to transport and power in the vicinity. Further updates will follow as the incident develops.

items.summary: Specialist resources attended Loughborough Town Hall following reports of a structural concern.
